text:
Maya: Heads-up: found a reproducible perf regression in the KV prefix cache benchmark when running a 64-thread replay. Hit rate falls from ~92% to ~68% after ~7m and p99 latency spikes ~3x.

Omar: Can you paste the exact replay command + config? want to try on my laptop.

Maya: sure — using the replay harness v2 with these params:
```
./replay --harness=prefix-kv --threads=64 --rps=800 --seed=42 \ 
  --trace-dir=/mnt/replays/apples/2026-03-12 --duration=900
```
config snippet:
```json
{
  "cache_size": 200000,
  "prefetch_policy": "prefix-v1",
  "batching": {"continuous": true, "max_batch": 128},
  "kernel_mode": "auto"
}
```

Liz: interesting — did you see eviction churn in the logs or just hit-rate drop?

Maya: eviction_count increases steadily after ~5m. logs show a lot of small TTL evictions + concurrent deletes. snippet:
```
[ks] INFO evicting prefix 0x1a2b, reason=cache_pressure, cur_size=205k
[ks] INFO put prefix 0x1a2b, cost=12ms
[ks] WARN concurrent_put detected for prefix 0x1a2b
```

Ben: could be a race between warmup and eviction under high concurrency. kernel selection + batching could change insertion timing and make hot prefixes get evicted.

perf-bot: Profile upload: s3://perf-uploads/1768654321/kv-prefix-64threads-profile.tar.gz (flamegraph + heap).

Omar: I ran a quick run with continuous batching disabled (continuous=false, max_batch=32) and hit-rate stayed ~90%. So batching seems to interact.

Maya: that matches what I see. But disabling batching increases CPU cost per token. We need to find the root cause not just workaround.

Liz: hypothesis: continuous batching increases concurrent KV put/get ordering which triggers suboptimal eviction because our LRU locks are coarse-grained. When many threads attempt to warm the same prefix, they do competing inserts and push eviction counters.

Ben: Can we repro with a synthetic microbenchmark that only exercises KV put/get ordering (no model kernels)? isolates kernel selection variable.

Maya: did that — synthetic KV harness shows the same eviction churn when parallelism >=48. When single-threaded or <=8 it’s stable.

srebot: Node metrics during run: 7m mark => ctx_switches spike, cpu_iowait low, memory free stable, minor swap activity.

Omar: notes from kernel selection side: the runtime chooses different matmul kernels based on batch shape; if kernel A is used, sequence of puts happens faster which increases insert rate. If kernel B used, insert rate slower and cache stays warmer. So it's timing-sensitive.

Maya: action plan I propose:
1) Add counters for concurrent_put backoff and per-prefix lock contention.
2) Run isolated KV-only microbench at multiple thread counts and report eviction vs contention.
3) Run apples-to-apples compare with kernel pinned to A vs B to measure timing effect.
4) Try a small change: make eviction sampling use estimation rather than immediate size after put to avoid immediate eviction churn.

Liz: +1. Also add an experiment to vary cache_size by +20% to see if it's purely elastic.

Omar: I'll pin kernels and run a 3x A/B on canary region tonight. Maya — can you add the contention counters to the harness?

Maya: Yep. I'll push a patch to the replay harness in ~30m. Patch includes a new metric stream (kv.lock_wait_ms, kv.concurrent_puts) and a short script to aggregate over windows.

Ben: small note: when aggregating, focus on unique prefix cardinality vs total puts — high duplicate prefixes mean warmup should succeed, but if cardinality increases then hit-rate will drop even without races.

Maya: good call. I'll include unique_prefix_count in the output.

perf-bot: quick diff summary for patch 1768654321: +120 -8 in replay/harness/kv_metrics.cpp. CI perf-tests queued.

Omar: thanks. If we confirm kernel timing is the trigger, we should consider a short-term mitigation: add a tiny randomized backoff on KV insert if lock contention > threshold. Low-risk and fast to roll.

Liz: agree. long-term: consider more fine-grained prefix locks or lock-free structures.

Maya: I'll post results here once I have the microbench numbers (expect ~2h). Leaving logs and raw traces in the perf S3 path.

Ben: thanks — ping @srebot if you want me to provision a few extra canary nodes for isolation.

srebot: allocated 3 canary nodes in us-west-2 for experiments (ids: canary-47, canary-48, canary-49).

Maya: perfect. Will run with and without continuous batching, pinned kernels A/B, and cache_size +/-20%.

Omar: awesome — this is looking actionable. :thumbsup:

Maya: closing for now; will reopen thread with numeric results.
